title: D-008: Seven QA Perspectives
body:
# D-008: Seven QA Perspectives

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

Quality assurance uses seven distinct evaluative perspectives: reader, skeptic, domain, style, coherence, ai-stink, and final (aggregator). Each perspective is a separate agent. The final agent issues ACCEPT / CONDITIONAL_ACCEPT / BLOCK.

## Why

Single-perspective QA misses systematic failure modes. A document can be clear to the reader but factually wrong (domain), stylistically correct but structurally incoherent (coherence), or convincing but full of AI-stink patterns. Separating perspectives prevents the common failure where a positive impression on one axis masks failures on another.

The seven perspectives were designed to cover the full range of document quality failures without overlap:
- **Reader:** Catches failures in intelligibility and assumed knowledge
- **Skeptic:** Catches failures in claim grounding and argument strength
- **Domain:** Catches failures in factual accuracy and canon compliance
- **Style:** Catches failures in style pack application and voice consistency
- **Coherence:** Catches failures in structure, logic flow, and internal consistency
- **AI-stink:** Catches the specific failure mode of machine-generated language patterns
- **Final (aggregator):** Synthesizes the six perspective outputs into a single gate verdict

The six non-aggregator perspectives can run in parallel, making the QA cycle efficient despite its depth. The final agent runs only after all six perspectives have completed.

## AI-Stink as a First-Class Perspective

Including ai-stink detection as a required QA step — not an optional pass — reflects the doctrine that "final text must feel written, not generated." This is a hard quality requirement, not a preference. Any framework that produces text can produce AI-stink patterns. Making it a first-class QA perspective ensures it is never skipped in the name of efficiency.

## Alternatives Considered

**Single comprehensive QA review.** Rejected: a single review cannot maintain seven evaluative mindsets simultaneously without allowing one to dominate. The reader perspective tends to dominate in single-reviewer contexts, causing skeptic and domain failures to be underweighted.

**Three-perspective QA** (reader, skeptic, style). Rejected: insufficient coverage. Coherence failures and AI-stink failures require dedicated perspectives. Domain failures require a perspective that holds canon knowledge, which is a distinct function from reader evaluation.

## Consequences

Running a full QA cycle is heavier than a single review pass. The orchestrate-review command parallelizes the first six perspectives and runs qa-final on aggregated results, making the overhead manageable. The QA infrastructure is a Phase 4 deliverable — all seven agents must be implemented before the full QA cycle can be run.
